edges.limitations: The model's vascular readout is an arterial pulse waveform change, which is a whole-animal haemodynamic measure. It is consistent with altered vascular tone but does not itself measure vasodilator or vasoconstrictor responses, and the authors state it as a suggestion rather than a demonstration. No equivalent human vascular measurement is reported.

A complete nephron deletion, not the in-frame deletion patients carry, and patients retain one wild-type allele. The same paper shows WNK4 degradation is restored when wild-type cullin-3 is present, so the heterozygous human state is not reproduced by the null.

Instead of the salt retention and hypertension of the human disease, these mice end up with salt-sensitive hypotension, hypochloraemic alkalosis and diabetes insipidus, with renal inflammation and fibrosis. Removing cullin-3 entirely from the nephron is toxic in ways the patient allele is not, so this model cannot stand in for the disease at the physiological level.

nodes.description: Overactive NCC reabsorbs sodium and chloride in the distal convoluted tubule. Because sodium delivered more distally is the driving force for potassium and hydrogen ion secretion in the collecting duct, taking it up earlier both expands volume and reduces the gradient available for potassium and acid excretion. This single step therefore produces the hypertension and the electrolyte picture together, and it is salt-dependent: dietary salt restriction alone improves it.

nodes.description: KLHL3, the substrate adaptor that presents WNK kinases to cullin-3, falls in abundance in the presence of CUL3-delta9. Degradation runs through both the proteasome and autophagy. In knock-in mice the fall is specific to KLHL3: other KLHL family proteins such as KLHL2 are unchanged. Because the adaptor is what recruits the substrate, losing it blocks WNK degradation even by the remaining wild-type cullin-3.

nodes.description: CUL3-delta9 loses its interaction with the COP9 signalosome, which deneddylates cullins, and with CAND1, which exchanges substrate adaptors. Cullin-RING ligase activity depends on cycling between neddylated and deneddylated states rather than on neddylation alone, so losing both regulators dysregulates the cycle. The direction of the resulting neddylation change is disputed in the literature and is recorded as an open question rather than asserted here.
